title: Grocery Receipt

origin.title: Photo of a Costco Wholesale receipt, Greenville SC, March 31 2019
origin.clearance_note: A phone photo of a shopper's Costco receipt, published as an editorial image on The Kitchn (Apartment Therapy Media) and downloaded by script from the publisher's image CDN as a 730x973 JPEG. The publisher is not the receipt's owner, so it was treated as a personal record: the two identifiers tied to the shopper were replaced in the pixels before parsing. The photo was wrapped in a one-page PDF with no text layer and no metadata. The store's address, item numbers and transaction references are the retailer's and were kept.

redactions.method: Pixels painted over with background blended from the paper on either side and redrawn in Arial Narrow at the original size and ink colour; the PDF is rebuilt from the edited image only

replaced.what: last four digits of the masked payment card

redactions.verified: Tesseract OCR of the output finds neither original, as literals or inside any run of digits; both stand-ins read back

notes: The request asked for a schema with a list of every item purchased, with name, quantity, unit price, total price and taxable status; the items array carries all five, plus the item number and the printed tax-code letter. No feature page or fields were requested. The overlay follows one item line across the receipt: its description, its price, and the 'E' tax flag in the left margin, then the 0.00 tax line that the flag explains and the total. quantity and unit_price are not printed on this receipt (one of each item); extraction fills them as 1 and the line total, grounded to the item line. taxable is an inference from the 'E' flag and grounds OFF to it, so it is not featured; the flag itself is.
